title: The past and present of a mute cricket: a re-understanding of the Goniogryllus Chopard, 1936 based on an integrative taxonomic study (Orthoptera: Gryllinae; Gryllini; Brachytrypina)
content:
Abstract
Goniogryllus is a genus within the subfamily Gryllinae, characterized primarily by the lack of sound-producing ability. Species of this genus are predominantly distributed in China, with only two species recorded from India and Japan. We explored the systematic status and relationships within Goniogryllus based on an integrative taxonomic study. The study revealed that Goniogryllus belongs to the subtribe Brachytrupina of the tribe Gryllini within the subfamily Gryllinae. It is sister to the winged and sound-producing genera Phonarellus and Vietacheta. Goniogryllus is divided into two species groups containing a total of 17 species, including six new species and three synonyms. Ancestral state reconstruction of the four wing types (apterous, micropterous, brachypterous, and macropterous) and analysis of distributional ranges within Goniogryllus show that Goniogryllus potamini Bey-Bienko, 1956, the only species with flight-capable wings, has a wide distribution that is not solely due to the migratory capabilities afforded by macropterous wings. Our study aims to explore the morphological diversity within the genus and to examine the common diagnostic characters shared by all its species, thereby providing a more comprehensive understanding of its taxonomy. Accurate species delimitation requires a comprehensive integration of morphological, geographic, and molecular data. Our research clarifies the systematic position of Goniogryllus, clarifies species relationships within the genus, and defines taxonomic characters and their application strategies. This will lay the foundation for future evolutionary and functional studies and contribute new insights to the study of wing polymorphic insects.
